item.title: India Chemical Shares Surge on Hormuz Disruption, Better Pricing
item.description: For the broader rally to sustain, demand will need to recover too.

item.title: Xi Vows to Make AI for All in Debut at China’s Top Tech Summit
item.description: President Xi Jinping hailed China’s progress in developing low-cost artificial intelligence, pressing his personal imprint on the country’s rapidly expanding global influence to call for a more open technological order.

item.title: Industrial Metals Decline as Traders Weigh Fed Rate Outlook
item.description: Base metals retreated on Friday as traders weighed the likelihood of higher interest rates and their negative impact on demand.

item.title: HDFC Bank, ICICI Bank Eye FX Deposits For Margin Boost
item.description: The Reserve Bank of India’s latest measures to attract foreign currency inflows are set to lift optimism when some of the country’s largest private sector banks report on Saturday.

item.title: Xi Pushes Human Oversight of AI as China Expands Global Outreach
item.description: Xi Pushes Human Oversight of AI as China Expands Global Outreach【原文：Xi Pushes Human Oversight of AI as China Expands Global Outreach】

item.title: Mitsubishi Electric Eyes Power-Chip Merger With Rohm and Toshiba
item.description: Mitsubishi Electric Corp. seeks to reach a deal by September with rivals Toshiba Corp. and Rohm Co. to combine their power semiconductor operations.

item.title: China Chip Stock Pullback Drives Investor Fear to Four-Year High
item.description: A measure of investor sentiment on China technology hardware is flashing its most bearish reading in over four years as the red-hot rally in chip stocks rapidly cools.

item.title: Tata Group Resorts to Older Tech to Launch Its Chip Foray
item.description: Tata Electronics Pvt. is preparing to make India’s first semiconductor wafers on far older technology than it originally expected, underscoring the challenges the country faces in trying to build a domestic chip industry from scratch.

item.title: Modi Adviser Urges India to Seek More Chinese Investment, Trade
item.description: India should deepen economic ties with Beijing by opening the door to greater Chinese investment and reconsidering regional trade pacts as shifting geopolitics make the US a less dependable partner, an adviser to Prime Minister Narendra Modi said.

item.title: Investor Srinivasan Seeks Meeting with Anwar’s Office After Raid
item.description: Investor Balaji Srinivasan requested a meeting with the office of Malaysian Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim, days after immigration officers raided his startup school in Forest City, a mega-development in the southern state of Johor.

item.title: Japan’s ‘Decisive Action’ Threat Does Little to Scare Yen Bears
item.description: Japan’s Finance Minister Satsuki Katayama used her strongest language in weeks to warn of possible intervention in the currency market, but did little to scare yen speculators as the currency continues to hover near its lowest level in four decades.

item.title: Taco Bell Pulls Lettuce in Some States After Cyclospora Outbreak
item.description: Taco Bell said it has voluntarily removed potentially affected lettuce from a supplier linked to a multistate Cyclospora outbreak and will replace the ingredient within 24 hours at restaurants in affected states.

item.title: DeepSeek Champions China’s Bid to Flood the World With Cheap AI
item.description: On a video conference call from Hangzhou earlier this year, one of China’s hottest startups held a four-hour pitch meeting with potential venture investors that was unusual by almost any measure. Only two representatives per institution were allowed. The majority of those present were getting a glimpse of the company’s leader for the very first time.

item.title: Chipmaker Kioxia’s Market Value Halves From Peak on AI Selloff
item.description: Japanese memory chipmaker Kioxia Holdings Corp.’s market capitalization halved in just a month since becoming the nation’s most valuable company, on growing concerns the AI-driven rally in the sector has gone too far.

item.title: China AI Stocks’ 1000%-Plus Profit Gain May Fail to Revive Rally
item.description: China’s artificial intelligence companies are poised to deliver robust earnings, but elevated expectations after a months-long rally are raising the bar for tech stocks to climb further.

item.title: Thai Stocks Go From Worst to Best as Funds Eye Further Gains
item.description: Thai stocks are finding favor again as investors bet that an Anutin Charnvirakul-led government will bring an end to years of political turbulence, spurring foreign capital inflows.

item.title: Gold Heads for Weekly Fall as Hormuz Strikes Raise Fed-Hike Bets
item.description: Gold was on track for the biggest weekly loss since early June as renewed hostilities in the Middle East raised the odds that the US Federal Reserve may need to raise interest rates to contain inflation.

item.title: Top Currency Forecaster Says Yen May Reach 170 Against Dollar
item.description: The most-accurate forecaster of dollar-yen in Bloomberg’s latest rankings sees the currency sliding as far as 170 against the dollar next year, using a prediction model that largely ignores the news and focuses on technical analysis instead.

item.title: Xi Seeks Global AI Sway as Model Power Spurs Security Alarm
item.description: President Xi Jinping rode the rise of China’s AI models to stake his claim to shape the technology’s global rules, even as their growing power stirs security alarm in Washington and Beijing alike.

item.title: Fed’s Jefferson Says Policy Well Positioned If Inflation Cools
item.description: Federal Reserve Vice Chair Philip Jefferson suggested the central bank should consider raising interest rates if inflation doesn’t cool soon, but said monetary policy is well positioned for now.

item.title: Intuitive Surgical Drops as ACA Changes, GLP-1s Weigh on Growth
item.description: Intuitive Surgical shares fell as much as 13% in after-market trading as growth in use of its da Vinci surgical robots slowed to the weakest pace in four years and its guidance for procedure growth was unchanged.

item.title: Bank Rally Hits Short Sellers Betting on Australia Lending Slump
item.description: The upward march in share prices of Australia’s biggest banks is reversing the tumble sparked two months ago by property tax changes, and inflicting pain on short sellers who were anticipating a prolonged plunge.

item.title: Asia Stocks to Track US Slide on Chipmaker Selloff: Markets Wrap
item.description: Stocks in Asia look set to open lower Friday after a selloff in chipmakers hit Wall Street amid concerns over whether massive artificial-intelligence investments will justify lofty valuations.

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for July 17
item.description: Oil extended a weekly advance as the escalating conflict between the US and Iran raised concerns about disruptions to supply from the Middle East.

item.title: Mozambique President Eyes China Debt Deal Modeled on Brazil Pact
item.description: Mozambique is making progress toward a debt restructuring deal with China similar to the one it reached with Brazil and is seeking a new International Monetary Fund program this year, President Daniel Chapo said.

item.title: CoreLogic in Talks to Sweeten Terms on Struggling Debt Sale
item.description: CoreLogic Inc. is considering offering sweeter terms on at least a portion of its $5.3 billion debt deal after receiving lukewarm investor demand.

item.title: How the Iran War Is Rewiring the Oil Market
item.description: The US-Israel war with Iran was supposed to blow up energy markets, but that hasn’t happened yet. In this weekly documentary, Bloomberg Originals explains why.

item.title: Making Sense of US Consumer Price Indexes, Jobs Numbers and Sentiment Surveys
item.description: On today’s Big Take podcast: We take stock of the US economy — what the latest data tell us, and what it misses about Americans’ financial reality.

item.title: Alcoa Shares Tumble After Cyclone Cuts Into Alumina Output
item.description: Alcoa Corp. cut its production forecast for alumina after operational problems at an Australian refinery weighed on output, overshadowing a quarter in which higher aluminum prices helped lift the metal producer’s revenue.

item.title: DeepMind CEO to Lobby Washington on Plan for Group to Vet AI Models
item.description: Earlier this week, Google DeepMind Chief Executive Officer Demis Hassabis unveiled a proposal for a new international watchdog that would do “rigorous” tests and reviews of cutting-edge AI models before release.
